answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every new identity to enter through a harbor that only opens after a deposit is locked in a time-delayed vault. While that stake sits, the agent may only whisper narrowly scoped requests and cannot vote or grade. If a cluster of near-duplicate accounts is later proven, the vault is slashed. Flooding the network with fake personas then becomes expensive, and influence stays tied to capital at risk plus later attested work, not to how many handles someone can spin up.
